text:
omar: Heads-up — I want to start a controlled rollout for the mixed-GPU spot strategy next week. Main goals: reduce cost by ~30% on batch jobs, avoid large disruption on inference pools, and ensure AMI rotation/tagging is consistent across launch templates.

jess: SGTM. high level plan?

omar: Plan: 1) Add weighted mixed_instances_policy to autoscaling groups, 2) publish new launch template versions with the interruption-handler systemd unit and preinstalled ssm-agent, 3) add a fallback rule to prefer on-demand if spot capacity < X, 4) standardize tags: redwood:pool, redwood:capacity-tier, redwood:ami-build. Rollout via canary ASG first (10% traffic).

liam: For (3) how are you detecting capacity < X? cloudwatch metric? allocation strategy?

omar: We'll use an allocation check in the lifecycle hook from the interruption-handler + ASG scaling policy. Also set aws_ec2_fleet AllocationStrategy = "capacity-optimized" and fallback to OnDemandOption in tf. Example TF snippet I'm prototyping:

```hcl
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "inference_mixed" {
  mixed_instances_policy {
    launch_template {
      launch_template_specification {
        launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.inference.id
        version = "$Latest"
      }
    }
    instances_distribution {
      on_demand_allocation_strategy = "prioritized"
      on_demand_base_capacity = 0
      on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 20
    }
    overrides = [
      { instance_type = "g5.12xlarge"  , weighted_capacity = 64 },
      { instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge", weighted_capacity = 256 },
      { instance_type = "a2-highgpu-1g" , weighted_capacity = 16 }
    ]
  }
  tags = [
    { key = "redwood:pool", value = "inference-gpu", propagate_at_launch = true },
    { key = "redwood:capacity-tier", value = "spot-mixed", propagate_at_launch = true }
  ]
}
```

jess: I like the weighted capacities. For AMI rotation are you baking different drivers per instance family or use one universal AMI?

omar: We're going to publish family-specific AMIs in the same account/region but keep the AMI id in SSM Parameter Store as /redwood/ami/inference/<family>. Launch template will reference the parameter at boot via user-data + ec2-metadata lookup. That avoids editing LT on every rotation.

maria: Regarding interruption handling — want to avoid thundering herd if many spots terminate. We should stagger graceful termination and drain pods. Suggest adding a jittered sleep in the handler and a central rate limiter (DynamoDB token bucket) that marks instance as draining to the scheduler.

omar: Agreed. Prototype handler:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# /opt/redwood/spot-interrupt.sh
INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id)
# mark draining via API
aws dynamodb update-item --table Drains --key "{\"i\":{\"S\":\"$INSTANCE_ID\"}}" --attribute-updates '{"state":{"Value":{"S":"draining"}}}'
# jitter
sleep $((RANDOM % 30))
# cordon and drain k8s node
kubectl cordon $HOSTNAME && kubectl drain $HOSTNAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# then shutdown
shutdown -h now
```

jess: Nice. One operational ask: add a terraform flag to opt-out of the fallback to on-demand per environment (dev/staging should always go spot-only).

omar: Yup that will be a variable in module: enable_on_demand_fallback = true/false. We'll default false for non-prod.

liam: Can we add a small smoke test step in CI that launches a 1-node canary ASG with the new LT and runs a curl against /health for 5 minutes? Would catch missing ssm-agent or bad kernel modules.

maria: Also add a tag redwood:rollout=<timestamp> on new LTs so we can query which ASGs use them during the rollout.

devops-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://redwood.internal/tasks/INFRA-1298 - assigned to @omar, due 2 days

jess: thumbs up :thumbsup: small nit — keep the AMI build id in tag "redwood:ami-build" (value = build-2026-03-15) so we can correlate.

omar: Will do. I'll open the tf MR today with the mixed_instances_policy, new tags, and the interruption-handler user-data. Starting with canary in us-west-2.

liam: Ping us when the MR is ready. happy to review the ASG/TF bits.

maria: I'll prototype the dynamo rate limiter and share metrics for termination spikes.

omar: Thanks all — aim to kick off canary on Monday morning.

devops-bot: reminder: weekly infra sync on Monday 09:30 PST includes rollout notes.
